name: adv_ppo_bad
title: PPO with a rollout buffer, GAE and a clipped objective - eight planted defects
origin: the defective twin of adv_ppo_clean, hardening round 1, 2026-09-13
note: `unsupported` rows are planted defects no rule's documented detection covers today; they are recorded so they can be promoted to `expected` the day a rule can see them. The scorer ignores the key, exactly as ACCURACY section 5 requires.

expected.defect: the policy head and the value head live in a plain Python list
expected.why: neither head is registered on the module, so optimizer.Adam(policy.parameters()) never sees them and the two heads stay at their initialisation for the whole run
the trunk carries nn.Dropout(0.1), so every evaluation episode is scored with 10% of the trunk activations dropped and the reported return is noise

expected.defect: the evaluation episodes are not wrapped in torch.no_grad()
expected.why: a full autograd graph is built for every step of every evaluation episode and then thrown away

expected.defect: the whole module is pickled instead of its state_dict
expected.why: the checkpoint carries the class path, so it stops loading as soon as the file is renamed or moved

expected.defect: nothing seeds torch, numpy or random; the only seed in the file is env.reset(seed=...), which seeds the gymnasium environment and nothing else
expected.why: the trunk initialisation, the action sampling and the minibatch permutation all move between runs, so the reported learning curve is not reproducible

expected.defect: the epoch loss is accumulated as a live tensor inside the minibatch loop
expected.why: total_loss is created at line 120, outside both loops, so every minibatch of every one of the ten epochs keeps its autograd graph alive until ppo_update returns

expected.defect: optimizer.step() at line 139 runs before loss.backward() at line 140, in the same block
expected.why: each update applies the previous minibatch's gradients, so the first update is pure noise and every later one is one minibatch stale

forbidden.why: loss.backward() at line 140 is outside every no_grad block; the two no_grad blocks are the rollout forward (line 82) and the bootstrap value (line 182)
no softmax is applied anywhere - the policy head feeds Categorical(logits=...) and the value loss is F.mse_loss
there is no binary cross-entropy of any kind in this project
every observation is built with torch.as_tensor(..., device=DEVICE) and the buffer allocates on the same device
DEVICE is chosen by torch.cuda.is_available() at line 17
there is no train/test split call in this project at all
ActorCritic.__init__ calls super().__init__() on its first line (line 33)

unsupported.symbol: for start in range(0, n, MINIBATCH)
unsupported.defect: the minibatch update never calls optimizer.zero_grad(), so gradients accumulate across every minibatch of every epoch
unsupported.why: MLV201's documented detection anchors on `the innermost for whose iterable's ValueRef is tagged LOADER`; a PPO minibatch loop iterates a range of index offsets, so the rule never reaches this loop. See finding DGRG-02.

unsupported.defect: neither the advantages nor the returns are detached, so the value head is trained through the bootstrap target as well as through the value loss
unsupported.why: no rule models `a target tensor reaching a loss without .detach()`; MLV212 is the nearest later-tier code and it is about reduction='none'.

unsupported.symbol: loss = policy_loss + VALUE_COEF * value_loss + ENTROPY_COEF * entropy
unsupported.defect: the entropy bonus is added instead of subtracted, so the objective minimises entropy and the policy collapses to one action
unsupported.why: sign errors inside a composed objective are not modelled by any rule in the catalog.
